title: Rotational 3D printing of active–passive filaments and lattices with programmable shape morphing
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the method of creating active-passive filaments and lattices with programmable shape morphing using rotational 3D printing.
2. Problem - It aims to address the challenge of replicating the complex shape-morphing behavior of natural filaments in synthetic materials.
3. Method - The approach utilizes rotational multimaterial 3D printing to directly encode intrinsic curvature and twist in multimaterial elastomeric filaments during fabrication.
4. Key Result - This method enables the independent control of bending and torsion at every cross-section of the filament, resulting in complex shape-morphing materials.
5. Takeaway - Thus, the key message of this paper is the development of shape-morphing materials with complex programmable responses for applications in adaptive, robotic, or deployable architectures.

title: Multi-material direct ink writing and co-sintering of gadolinium oxide – zirconium oxide components
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the fabrication methods for multi-material ceramic composites.
2. Problem - It aims to resolve issues arising from the co-sintering of multi-material ceramic parts.
3. Method - The approach involves direct ink writing (DIW) and slurry optimization to align sintering kinetics.
4. Key Result - A reduction of over 10% in sintering mismatch was achieved with a combination of Gd2O3 and ZrO2.
5. Takeaway - The importance of optimized slurry formulations and continuous material gradients to minimize sintering mismatch is highlighted.

title: Functionally graded SS316L/Inconel 625 fabricated by SLM: the effects of remelting and ultrasonic burnishing on pore topology, surface integrity and electrochemical properties
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the fabrication of functionally graded materials (FGMs) combining SS316L and Inconel 625 via selective laser melting (SLM).
2. Problem - It aims to solve issues such as interfacial porosity, surface roughness, and corrosion susceptibility to enhance structural integrity and electrochemical performance.
3. Method - The study utilized an SLM platform to fabricate FGM specimens and applied in situ remelting and ultrasonic-assisted ball burnishing (UAB) as optimization techniques.
4. Key Result - Remelting significantly reduced porosity from 6.1% to 1.7%, and UAB improved surface roughness from 6.3 µm to 1.5 µm, enhancing electrochemical performance.
5. Takeaway - This research presents an innovative approach by integrating remelting with UAB to improve the performance of SS316L/Inconel 625 FGMs produced via SLM.

title: Data-Driven Design Space Analysis for Multimaterial Thermoplastic Composites Manufactured by Fused Filament Fabrication
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the design space analysis for multimaterial thermoplastic composites.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the challenge of increasingly complex design due to the sophistication of manufacturing processes and materials.
3. Method - The study utilized a commercially available fused filament fabrication printer and analyzed experimental data with truncated singular value decomposition.
4. Key Result - 97.8% of the variance in the stress-strain curves of samples was captured by the first component, indicating that composite strength can be controlled by manipulating reinforcement mass fraction.
5. Takeaway - It is crucial to recognize that the shape of nonlinear behavior remains largely fixed despite changes in reinforcement geometry when developing multimaterial systems.

title: Smart Operation Platform for Railway Rolling Stock Production Using Digital Twin and AI
venue: International Journal of Precision Engineering and Manufacturing-Green Technology
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a smart operation platform for railway rolling stock production using digital twin and AI.
2. Problem - Existing digital twin platforms primarily focus on monitoring or post-validation, lacking support for operational decisions during unexpected disruptions.
3. Method - The study proposes a digital twin-based platform that integrates AI-enabled real-time monitoring, discrete-event simulation, and AI-driven scheduling optimization.
4. Key Result - The proposed platform effectively manages delay propagation and stabilizes workload distribution while significantly improving throughput.

title: Single-parameter programmed thermomechanical actuation via 3D-printed helical director fields in liquid crystal elastomers
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses single-parameter programmed thermomechanical actuation using helical director fields in liquid crystal elastomers.
2. Problem - Conventional 3D printing methods restrict molecular alignment to a uniaxial path, necessitating complex multi-material architectures.
3. Method - A rotational 3D printing approach is employed to embed a helical director field within LCE filaments, allowing for multimodal actuation controlled by the helix angle.
4. Key Result - Adjusting the helix angle enables each filament to contract, elongate, twist, or remain unchanged when heated, decoupling actuation from geometry.
5. Takeaway - This research establishes a paradigm of material-encoded programmability, highlighting the potential for monolithic soft robots and reconfigurable structures.

title: Optimization of Mechanical Manufacturing Process Based on Digital Twin Technology
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the optimization of mechanical manufacturing processes based on digital twin technology.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the need for higher flexibility, efficiency, and cost reduction in the manufacturing industry.

5. Takeaway - This research provides technical solutions for real-time and precise optimization of mechanical manufacturing processes.

title: Multimodal Layer‐Crossing Interrogation of Brain Circuits Enabled by Microfluidic Axialtrodes
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper introduces a microfluidic axialtrode for multimodal interrogation of brain circuits.
2. Problem - It aims to address the limitation of conventional optical fibers that restrict spatial resolution due to their interaction with neural tissue only at the tip.
3. Method - The study develops a flexible neural interface that utilizes thermally drawn multimaterial fibers to achieve axial redistribution of integrated electrodes and microfluidic channels.
4. Key Result - This design enables spatially distributed optogenetics, multisite electrophysiological recording, and targeted drug delivery, allowing simultaneous interaction with multiple neuronal layers.
5. Takeaway - The axialtrode positions itself as a scalable and versatile platform for next-generation neural interfacing.

title: Mixing‐Driven Defects and Composition Evolution in Multi‐Material Metal Additive Manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses mixing-driven defects and composition evolution in multi-material metal additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - The reliable process design is limited by a lack of understanding of mixing-induced instabilities and defect formation.
3. Method - The study combines operando synchrotron X-ray radiography with high-fidelity multi-material multiphysics modeling.
4. Key Result - It demonstrates that material mixing fundamentally alters the stability of the keyhole, leading to composition-driven shape transitions and large pore formation.
5. Takeaway - The research establishes a validated mechanistic framework for multi-material LPBF and provides a quantitative basis for process optimization towards defect-controlled, compositionally graded manufacturing.

title: Interfacial structure − property relationships in additively manufactured WC-Co/316L multi-material systems
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper explores the relationships between interfacial structure and properties in multi-material additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to address the lack of reliable design principles for joining dissimilar materials with significant thermophysical mismatches.
3. Method - The study combined binder-jet WC-Co substrates with electron beam powder bed fusion deposited 316L stainless steel to investigate the interfacial characteristics.
4. Key Result - Findings revealed bidirectional elemental diffusion and a chemically graded transition region, with cracking occurring in the WC-Co substrate due to thermal stress mismatches.
5. Takeaway - The results provide insights for designing robust interfaces in multi-material additive manufacturing systems.

title: From printed architectures to functional batteries: printing technologies, post-processing, and sintering
ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - It aims to address the issue that the electrochemical functionality of 3D-printed structures is not solely determined by design and that post-processing is essential.
3. Method - It systematically summarizes various 3D printing technologies, including direct ink writing, electrohydrodynamic printing, fused deposition modeling, stereolithography, and binder jet printing.

5. Takeaway - By elucidating the intrinsic connection between 3D printing and sintering-based post-processing, it provides practical guidelines for the rational design and scalable fabrication of high-performance 3D-printed energy storage devices.

title: A Digital-Twin-Enabled AI-Driven Adaptive Planning Platform for Sustainable and Reliable Manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses an adaptive manufacturing planning platform enabled by digital twin and artificial intelligence.
2. Problem - Traditional manufacturing planning structures are fixed and deterministic, limiting the efficient optimization of operational stability and environmental sustainability in unpredictable situations.
3. Method - The study employs a method that combines a physics-based digital twin with a multi-objective proximal policy optimization algorithm to co-optimize reliability and sustainability indicators in real-time.
4. Key Result - A statistically significant improvement was achieved with 96.8% schedule performance and 84.7% OEE enhancement over 10,000 stochastic simulation experiments and a 12-week industrial pilot deployment.
5. Takeaway - This research provides a robust framework for adaptive, resilient, and eco-friendly manufacturing processes aligned with Industry 5.0 ideologies.

ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the development of tumor organoids using 3D bioprinting and its application in precision oncology.

title: 3D micropatterning of PEDOT:PSS/Gelatin conductive hydrogels via two-photon lithography for soft bioelectronics
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the creation of soft bioelectronic interfaces by blending PEDOT:PSS with gelatin.
2. Problem - Existing conductive structures are mechanically rigid compared to biological tissues, limiting cell-device interfacing.
3. Method - The authors employed two-photon lithography to micropattern a hydrogel made from PEDOT:PSS and methacrylate-modified gelatin.
4. Key Result - The resulting conductive hydrogels exhibited reduced electrical impedance and soft mechanical properties at both macro and micro scales.
5. Takeaway - This work highlights the potential for developing soft neural interfaces with biomimetic architectures that enhance electrical and mechanical integration.

2. Problem - It aims to solve the issue of insufficient adhesion between mechanically dissimilar 3D-printed materials, which leads to premature debonding under load.
3. Method - The study employs optimized printing orientations to create dense mechanical interlocking.

5. Takeaway - Thus, the core message is that strategic selection of printing orientation combined with interfacial mechanical design provides a scalable route for achieving robust bonding in multimaterial additive manufacturing.

5. Takeaway - Thus, the paper emphasizes the potential to enhance accuracy and efficiency in additive manufacturing across various materials through optimization of multi-layer structures.

title: A generalized printing process window for preventing surface overcuring in volumetric additive manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses a generalized printing process window for preventing surface overcuring in volumetric additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the issue of surface overcuring caused by misalignment of material, process, and hardware parameters.
3. Method - A generalized theoretical model was developed to predict spatial light-dose distribution within rotating ink and to investigate the effects of key physical parameters.
4. Key Result - The study demonstrated that surface overcuring can be effectively suppressed by lowering material absorbance, reducing vat diameters, and narrowing projection beams.

title: Two‐Photon Polymerized Poly(ε‐caprolactone) Microstructures with Shape‐Memory Behavior Under Compressive Loading
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses poly(ε-caprolactone) microstructures exhibiting shape-memory behavior under compressive loading.
2. Problem - Integrating shape memory properties into 3D-printed microstructures remains challenging due to existing systems lacking sufficient resolution or mechanical robustness at the microscale.
3. Method - The study develops a poly(ε-caprolactone) material crosslinked via thiol-ene chemistry to fabricate mechanically stable 3D microstructures using two-photon polymerization.
4. Key Result - The printed microstructures, weighing 0.89 µg, demonstrate excellent shape memory behavior, fully recovering their original shape even after significant compressive loads.
5. Takeaway - The research confirms that shape memory functionality can reliably transition from macro to microscale while maintaining structural integrity.

5. Takeaway - The findings highlight a significant advancement in the autonomy and versatility of electronics-free soft robots.

title: Next-Generation Biomedical Microwave Antennas: Metamaterial Design and Advanced Printing Manufacturing Techniques
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the design of next-generation biomedical microwave antennas using metamaterials and advanced printing techniques.
2. Problem - The performance of biomedical antennas faces challenges due to impedance detuning, signal absorption, and size constraints caused by proximity to the human body.
3. Method - Various manufacturing methods, including 3D printing, inkjet, aerosol jet, and screen printing, are employed to create conductive traces on textiles, elastomers, and biodegradable substrates.
4. Key Result - The study demonstrates that metamaterial and metasurface concepts enhance antenna miniaturization, gain, and isolation from lossy biological tissues.
5. Takeaway - The integration of novel materials and engineered electromagnetic structures paves the way for biomedical antennas that support future developments in unobtrusive monitoring and wireless implants.

title: MXene-Assembled Liquid Metal Hybrid Microparticles for Multifunctional and Stretchable Printed Electronics
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses MXene-assembled liquid metal hybrid microparticles for multifunctional and stretchable printed electronics.
2. Problem - It aims to address the challenge of integrating liquid metals into multifunctional electronic devices due to their limited functionality.
3. Method - The approach involves the self-assembly of MXene nanosheets around liquid metal microparticles to create an interconnected hybrid network.
4. Key Result - The hybrid microparticles activate electrical conductivity at a minimal strain of 2.5%, achieving high conductivity of 3.7 × 10^5 S/m and excellent stretchability of ~700%.
5. Takeaway - This study presents versatile material units that advance stretchable and integrated electronic systems.

title: Low‐Profile, High‐Gain GRIN RF Lenses via Multi‐Material Vat Photopolymerization
ai_summary_en:

4. Key Result - The resulting low-profile lenses achieved gain enhancements of up to 18 dB across the 10-18 GHz range.
5. Takeaway - Multi-material additive manufacturing can enhance signal gain in telecommunication devices while reducing their size.

ai_summary_en:

3. Method - The authors propose a method to redistribute internal stress in magnetostrictive materials by adjusting laser stimulation parameters and scanning strategies.

5. Takeaway - Thus, the core message of this paper is that the dynamically controlled printing method for magnetostrictive materials can overcome deformation limitations in large-scale applications.

5. Takeaway - The core message is that integrating physics into a data-driven optimization framework paves the way for autonomous and intelligent MEW systems.

title: Inverse modeling and design of additively manufactured hybrid acoustic metamaterials for low-frequency absorption
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the inverse modeling and design of hybrid acoustic metamaterials for low-frequency absorption.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the lack of a systematic approach for designing metamaterials suitable for low-frequency noise management.
3. Method - An inverse design framework is proposed to develop optimal hybrid metamaterials considering 3D printing constraints.

5. Takeaway - The paper emphasizes the importance of integrating inverse design with manufacturing-aware optimization for developing high-performance tunable acoustic metamaterials.

title: Intensity adjustment of tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing projection image sets
venue: Advanced Fabrication Technologies for Micro/Nano Optics and Photonics XIX
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses intensity adjustment of projection image sets in Tomographic Volumetric Additive Manufacturing (TVAM).
2. Problem - It aims to resolve issues related to long print times and failures in low-power TVAM systems caused by low mean intensity.
3. Method - The study investigates the effects of linear intensity scaling and saturation on printability and quality.
4. Key Result - An optimal saturation level of 8% yielded the highest print quality, achieving a Jaccard Similarity Index of 0.84.
5. Takeaway - The findings highlight that linear intensity scaling enhances printability and quality in low-power TVAM, while excessive saturation can degrade geometric fidelity.

ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - Conventional patterning methods are limited by high equipment costs and monotonous color outputs, hindering widespread adoption.
3. Method - A novel multi-color patterning method based on light-induced chemical crosslinking is proposed.
4. Key Result - The structural color hydrogels created using this method can display multi-color patterns with a minimum line width of 15μm, significantly enhancing their information-carrying capacity.

title: Hybrid path planning method for PCB drilling based on feature-aware and zone-optimization strategy
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the path optimization problem in drilling printed circuit boards.
2. Problem - The traditional Traveling Salesman Problem model has limitations when applied to circuit boards with high density and repetitive hole patterns.
3. Method - A hybrid path optimization algorithm is proposed by analyzing spatial distribution features of holes and employing a hierarchical optimization strategy.
4. Key Result - The proposed method significantly reduces both the total drilling path length and computation time compared to conventional optimization methods.
5. Takeaway - The key message of this paper is the necessity for a new path optimization approach to enhance drilling efficiency for high-density circuit boards.

5. Takeaway - This work establishes an integrated route to high-performance and geometry-programmable energy-absorbing LCEs.

title: Experimental mechanician for plate lattice metamaterial discovery
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the experimental mechanician for the discovery of plate lattice metamaterials.
2. Problem - Optimizing plate lattice metamaterials is challenging due to the presence of many parameters and multiple objectives.
3. Method - The study employs an experimental mechanician (ExMech) that integrates a robotic platform with a multi-objective active learning framework.
4. Key Result - ExMech establishes Pareto-optimal combinations in 25 iterations, improving compressive and shear yield strengths by 15.6% and 12.0%, respectively.
5. Takeaway - This research presents a self-optimizing experimental approach for plate lattice discovery, accelerating the identification of new mechanical metamaterials.

title: Experimental investigation of the thermal history in FDM-based 4D printing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper investigates the thermal history in FDM-based 4D printing.
2. Problem - There are limitations in understanding how thermal history affects layer-wise pre-strain and shape change during the printing process.
3. Method - The study quantifies the cooling of a single printed line by varying parameters such as nozzle temperature, printing speed, cooling fan, and build plate temperature, and analyzes the thermal history of multilayer structures.
4. Key Result - Thermal history plays a crucial role in pre-strain formation, with lower nozzle temperatures leading to increased shrinkage and curvature.
5. Takeaway - The control of thermal history during the printing process is essential for enhancing the performance of 4D printing.

title: Dual-wavelength photoinhibition-aided vat photopolymerization (PinVPP) of bio-based polymers and functional hydrogels
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the use of dual-wavelength photoinhibition-aided vat photopolymerization (PinVPP) for bio-based polymers and functional hydrogels.
2. Problem - It aims to address the challenges of limited control over photopolymerization kinetics that lead to issues like overcuring and mechanical fragility in bio-based materials.
3. Method - The approach involves using a lab-developed PinVPP platform to independently regulate radical generation and curing confinement by decoupling visible-light initiation from UV-triggered inhibition.
4. Key Result - The results demonstrate that PinVPP effectively reduces excessive cure thickness and enhances surface quality and mechanical consistency in resin systems.
5. Takeaway - The study indicates that PinVPP provides a scalable pathway for additive manufacturing of sustainable polymers and functional hydrogels by introducing tunable kinetic control.

title: DLP 4D Printing of Programmable Molecularly‐Engineered Liquid Crystal Elastomer Actuators
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the DLP 4D printing technology for programmable molecularly-engineered liquid crystal elastomer actuators.
2. Problem - Existing direct ink writing methods have limitations in resolution and geometric complexity, hindering effective alignment of liquid crystals.
3. Method - A two-stage photo-crosslinking approach was employed, where partially cured structures are mechanically programmed and then photo-crosslinked to fix mesogen alignment.
4. Key Result - This method enabled the fabrication of monodomain nematic LCEs with tunable thermo-mechanical properties and programmable actuation strains up to 45%.
5. Takeaway - The DLP approach demonstrates potential as an attractive alternative to DIW for the fabrication of functional soft actuators.

title: Compressive Response and Energy Absorption of Additively Manufactured Elastomers with Varied Simple Cubic Architectures
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper investigates the compressive response and energy absorption characteristics of additively manufactured elastomers with varied simple cubic architectures.
2. Problem - There is a lack of comprehensive data on the compressive behavior of elastomers, particularly regarding structure-property relationships.
3. Method - The study analyzes the mechanical response of polyurethane-based simple cubic structures by varying volume fraction, unit cell length, and patterning.
4. Key Result - Increasing the volume fraction from 10% to 50% resulted in significant changes in compressive stress-strain performance and a 3962.5% increase in energy absorption density.
5. Takeaway - The findings provide a foundation for understanding how structural design aspects influence the performance of elastomeric cellular materials.

title: Chemical and Mechanical Evolution of a Volumetric Additive Manufacturing (VAM) Resin Under High-Temperature Storage
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the chemical and mechanical evolution of volumetric additive manufacturing (VAM) resin under high-temperature storage.
2. Problem - It aims to resolve the insufficient understanding of how resin storage history affects VAM process stability.
3. Method - The study investigates the changes in a representative acrylate-based VAM resin subjected to accelerated thermal aging, analyzing various properties.
4. Key Result - While molecular weight remained stable, significant changes in mechanical and dimensional properties were observed in the aged resins.
5. Takeaway - Aging of resin should be explicitly considered in manufacturing, and routine monitoring and recalibration are recommended to enhance VAM reproducibility.

ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - It aims to address the limitations of existing vascular stents and advance minimally invasive cardiovascular therapies.
3. Method - Microarchitected coronary artery stents were fabricated using projection micro-stereolithography (PµSL) 4D printing with a polycaprolactone-based shape memory polymer composite.
4. Key Result - The stents can rapidly and autonomously recover shape under physiological conditions without external heating, maintaining a favorable balance between mechanical flexibility and strength.
5. Takeaway - This work presents the potential for adaptive vascular stents with programmable thermoresponsive behavior and intelligent deployment for personalized treatment.

title: Achieving superior thermal stability in vat photopolymerized silica-based ceramic cores via kyanite-induced expansion compensation
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a novel method for fabricating complex ceramic cores used in aero-engines.
2. Problem - The performance of existing silica-based ceramic cores is limited by excessive sintering shrinkage and high-temperature deformation.
3. Method - The study systematically analyzed the effects of introducing kyanite into the silica-based ceramic core.
4. Key Result - When kyanite content exceeded 15 wt.%, sintering shrinkage was effectively inhibited, achieving optimal performance.
5. Takeaway - The findings demonstrate that utilizing kyanite can significantly enhance the performance of silica-based ceramic cores.

title: 3D-printed CF-PLA bone plates with metamaterial structures: Design, fabrication, and mechanical evaluation
venue: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials/Journal of mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the design, fabrication, and mechanical performance of 3D-printed carbon fiber-reinforced polylactic acid (CF-PLA) bone plates with metamaterial structures.
2. Problem - It aims to address the limitations of traditional metallic bone plates and the issue of stress shielding.
3. Method - The study employed Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) to fabricate various lattice-structured bone plates and evaluate their mechanical properties.
4. Key Result - The tetrachiral structure exhibited superior bending capacity and strength, indicating that CF-PLA metamaterial plates could effectively reduce stiffness and promote bone healing compared to metal plates.
5. Takeaway - 3D-printed CF-PLA metamaterial structures present a promising alternative to metallic bone plates, with potential for patient-specific implant development.

ai_summary_en:

5. Takeaway - Integrating rotational actuators can significantly improve penetration efficiency in robotic systems for subsurface exploration.

title: Time Code for multifunctional 3D printhead controls
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper proposes a time-based synchronization method called Time Code (T-Code) for multifunctional 3D printhead controls.
2. Problem - The existing G-Code has limitations in integrating auxiliary control commands without disrupting the print path.
3. Method - T-Code decouples auxiliary control from G-Code, allowing for uninterrupted enrichment of print paths.
4. Key Result - This method reduces defects, enhances print speed, and minimizes the mechanical burden on 3D printers.
5. Takeaway - Thus, the paper presents a new approach for rapidly creating complex multimaterial structures in 3D printing.

title: The Influence of Print Orientation and Discontinuous Carbon Fiber Content on the Tensile Properties of Selective Laser-Sintered Polyamide 12
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the effects of print orientation and discontinuous carbon fiber content on the tensile properties of selectively laser-sintered polyamide 12.
2. Problem - It aims to address the limitations of the benefits of discontinuous fibers in enhancing material properties due to print and fiber orientation.
3. Method - The study analyzed tensile and fracture properties using horizontal and vertical specimens with varying contents of discontinuous carbon fibers.
4. Key Result - Vertical specimens with increased fiber content showed reduced tensile strength and consistency, while horizontal specimens exhibited the opposite trend.
5. Takeaway - The key message is that selecting print orientation can help tune the properties and improve the functionality of fiber-reinforced parts produced by selective laser sintering.

ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the 3D printing of soft composites with tunable visco-hyperelastic properties.
2. Problem - There is a need to precisely control the spatially varying properties of soft materials due to the limitations of existing high-cost methods.
3. Method - Novel soft composites are fabricated using low-cost extrusion-based additive manufacturing, employing a customized 3D printer to adjust hyperelastic properties through reinforcement patterns.
4. Key Result - A method for efficiently modeling the design-property relationships of these composites has been developed, enabling the realization of composites with designed property variations.
5. Takeaway - This research opens up possibilities for the precise manufacturing of soft structures with tunable visco-hyperelastic properties for various applications.

title: Towards a digital twin of extrusion-based additive manufacturing: an experimentally validated numerical model of ironing process
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the development of a digital twin for extrusion-based additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the issue of porosity while reducing manufacturing time and enhancing quality.
3. Method - A multiphase non-Newtonian computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation was used to optimize ironing post-processing parameters under various extrusion temperatures and layer heights.
4. Key Result - Ironing resulted in a reduction of manufacturing time by up to 31.97% and an improvement in ultimate tensile strength by up to 21.49%.
5. Takeaway - The study lays the groundwork for a reliable CFD model that can support the creation of a digital twin for MEX.

title: Topology and Toolpath Optimization-Inspired Toolpath Planning for Continuous Fiber Material Extrusion
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses topology and toolpath optimization for continuous fiber material extrusion.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the issue of poor-quality toolpaths generated by existing alignment-based material extrusion slicers that strictly adhere to optimized geometry boundaries.
3. Method - The approach employs Bézier splines to softly fit toolpaths to the optimized design while allowing manual editing for manufacturability.
4. Key Result - Toolpaths generated using the proposed method maintain high continuity and alignment, providing consistently spaced deposition paths compared to other alignment-based techniques.
5. Takeaway - The core message of this paper is the introduction of a new toolpath planning approach that allows for manual adjustments to optimized designs for improved manufacturability.

title: Selective infusion of spatially controlled domains via vat photopolymerization 3D-printing for chemically diverse multimaterial parts
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a method for creating multimaterial parts through selective infusion of spatially controlled domains.
2. Problem - It aims to address the challenges of transitioning between liquid resins and processing incompatibilities among material classes in multimaterial object fabrication.
3. Method - The authors developed a technique called infusion multimaterial actinic spatial control additive manufacturing (iMASC-AM) using dual wavelength light projection.
4. Key Result - The iMASC-AM method demonstrated the ability to infuse various organic dyes, silicone resins, and metal salts, enabling the fabrication of functional circuits with distinct conductive and insulating properties in a single print.
5. Takeaway - The key message of this paper is that the iMASC-AM method opens up possibilities for creating chemically diverse multimaterial parts that are generally inaccessible through traditional vat photopolymerization.

title: Scan and 3D Print: Magnetic Resonance Imaging‐Guided, Monolithic Desktop Fabrication of Highly Biomimetic Skeletal System of the Human Hand
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a method for creating a biomimetic skeletal system of the human hand using MRI data for patient-specific 3D printing.
2. Problem - Existing 3D-printed hand models often fail to replicate the unique functionalities of biological hands.
3. Method - The study employs MRI data to create CAD models and utilizes a monolithic 3D printing approach with a low-cost desktop printer.
4. Key Result - The resulting hand demonstrates several unique behaviors of natural hands and shows potential for custom prosthetic hand production.
5. Takeaway - This paper presents an innovative method for producing highly functional biomimetic hands using affordable desktop 3D printing technology.

5. Takeaway - The paper emphasizes the potential of rotary additive manufacturing technology to overcome the limitations of traditional manufacturing.

ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses real-time synchronization issues in robotic digital twins within smart manufacturing.
2. Problem - It seeks to resolve inconsistencies in data exchange between physical robots and their digital counterparts caused by network latency and interoperability challenges.
3. Method - The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to analyze relevant research and categorize synchronization barriers and technical solutions.
4. Key Result - The findings reveal six primary synchronization challenges and six corresponding solution clusters.
5. Takeaway - The synchronization of robotic digital twins is a complex coordination issue that necessitates a holistic system design approach.

5. Takeaway - Advancements in NDT technologies can lead to a transformation into an intelligent and integrated quality assurance system for composite material manufacturing.

title: Multi-agent cooperative swarm learning for dynamic layout optimisation of reconfigurable robotic assembly cells based on digital twin
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses a multi-agent cooperative swarm learning framework for dynamic layout optimization of reconfigurable robotic assembly cells.
2. Problem - Current research simplifies layout design, addressing issues like overlap and transportation distance in an approximate manner.
3. Method - It utilizes a 3D digital representation based on a digital twin in a proposed learning environment and applies a decentralized multi-agent cooperative swarm learning approach.
4. Key Result - In the first use case, layout compactness was reduced by 3.8 times, production time decreased by 2.3 times, and rearrangement costs dropped by 33.4%.
5. Takeaway - The paper demonstrates that the dynamic layout optimization framework allows for flexible adjustment of manufacturing objectives.

5. Takeaway - Thus, the core message of this paper is the potential of an innovative printing technology to implement diverse material properties in a single fabrication step.

title: Strain and damage sensing performance of functionally graded nanocomposite lattices enabled by DLP 3D printing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the strain and damage sensing performance of functionally graded nanocomposite lattices enabled by DLP 3D printing.
2. Problem - It aims to overcome the limitations of energy absorption and strain sensing performance in existing nanocomposite lattice structures.
3. Method - Geometrically graded octet and kelvin lattices were fabricated using DLP additive manufacturing, and their mechanical and piezoresistive properties were analyzed.
4. Key Result - The graded octet lattice showed up to 2.6 times improvement in energy absorption compared to its non-graded counterpart, along with enhanced piezoresistive characteristics.
5. Takeaway - The study suggests that incorporating functional geometric gradients in nanocomposite lattices can enhance energy absorption and strain/damage sensing capabilities under various loading conditions.

venue: 2025 IEEE 8th International Conference on Soft Robotics (RoboSoft)
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses soft and highly-integrated optical fiber bending sensors for proprioception in multi-material 3D printed fingers.
2. Problem - Existing integration methods are cumbersome and require manual steps, limiting efficient sensor production.
3. Method - A semi-automated printing process is employed to embed plastic optical fibers with readout electronics in 3D printed flexures.
4. Key Result - The sensors achieve an average of 70% linearity and 4.81° RMS error, maintaining fingertip position estimation accuracy of 12 mm under external forces.
5. Takeaway - This research presents an efficient sensor integration method to enhance proprioceptive capabilities in soft robotics.

1. Topic - This paper addresses the interplay between element mixing, intermetallics, and microcracks in multi-material laser additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to understand and resolve the issues of microcrack formation and intermetallic compound development in existing manufacturing processes.
3. Method - An experimental approach and analytical techniques were used to investigate the effects of element mixing and elucidate the mechanisms of microcrack formation.
4. Key Result - It was found that the mixing of elements and the formation of intermetallic compounds play a crucial role in the occurrence of microcracks.
5. Takeaway - Therefore, considering the interactions between element mixing and intermetallic compounds is essential for improving quality in multi-material additive manufacturing.

title: Reinforcement learning-enabled design of topological interlocking materials for sustainable multi-material additive manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the design of topological interlocking materials for multi-material additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to solve issues related to printability and environmental considerations, particularly the recyclability of composite structures in multi-material AM.
3. Method - A computational interlocking design strategy utilizing Q-learning in reinforcement learning is employed to optimize the spatial arrangement of materials in a 3D design space.
4. Key Result - The findings demonstrate a pathway towards sustainable, reusable, and recyclable multi-material additive manufacturing.
5. Takeaway - Ultimately, this paper offers new possibilities for circular manufacturing and resource-efficient design.

title: Rapid and Inexpensive Image‐Guided Grayscale Biomaterial Customization via <scp>LCD</scp> Printing
venue: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research Part A
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a method for customizing biomaterials using low-cost LCD printing.
2. Problem - Traditional 3D printing technologies have limitations in spatially adjusting the physicochemical properties of biomaterials.
3. Method - The study proposes a method that processes grayscale images using an inexpensive LCD printer to adjust the chemical and mechanical properties of biomaterials.
4. Key Result - The approach demonstrates the ability to spatially control the photochemical properties of various biomaterials.
5. Takeaway - This research suggests that low-cost biomaterial customization technology could be beneficial for biological studies and functional tissue engineering.

title: Projection-Based Simulation Method for Robotic 3D Printing of Large-Scale Polymer Composite Structures
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a projection-based simulation method for robotic 3D printing.
2. Problem - It aims to address the issue of existing finite element methods oversimplifying material anisotropy caused by printing paths.
3. Method - The study employs a projection-based approach that directly maps toolpath-defined fiber orientations into a finite element model.
4. Key Result - The mechanical properties of printed carbon fiber-reinforced ABS were experimentally validated, showing a 5% difference in predicted mid-span deflection from experimental measurements.
5. Takeaway - This method offers a scalable approach for accurate simulation of FDM-printed composites.

title: Physics-based model for dot geometry prediction in dot-by-dot wire arc additive manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses a geometric prediction model for dot-by-dot wire arc additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to resolve the impact of dot geometry on optimal welding paths and the mechanical properties of the final product.
3. Method - An analytical physics-based geometrical model is proposed, which is applicable to various scenarios and materials based on heat transfer and mass conservation.
4. Key Result - Preliminary experimental validation on ER70S-6 steel bars showed fair accuracy in predicting the diameter and height of the bars.
5. Takeaway - The core message of this paper is that a physics-based model is useful for predicting the geometric characteristics in dot-by-dot additive manufacturing.

title: Phase-separation-driven cracking in additive manufacturing of Ni-Cu alloy systems
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the cracking mechanism in additive manufacturing of Ni-Cu alloy systems.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the issue of crack formation during the laser powder-bed fusion of CuCrZr and IN625.
3. Method - Operando X-ray diffraction and imaging experiments were used to investigate the liquid immiscibility between the two alloy systems.
4. Key Result - The highest crack susceptibility was found in the 20-40 wt.% CuCrZr-IN625 composition range.
5. Takeaway - The cracking mechanism explained in this study can be extended to other Cu-Ni alloy combinations that induce immiscibility when mixed with Cu.

4. Key Result - It highlights the potential for innovative path planning techniques to optimize additive manufacturing processes.
5. Takeaway - The core message is that path planning techniques play a crucial role in enhancing the quality and efficiency of additive manufacturing.

4. Key Result - The study establishes a comprehensive relationship between geometric design and mechanical response, demonstrating the interplay between bending angle and stiffness through experiments.
5. Takeaway - This research highlights the potential of multimaterial 3D printing techniques in developing flexible and adaptive robotic structures.

title: One-Vat Multimaterial 3D Printing: The Devil is in the Details
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses 3D printing technology that utilizes multiple materials in a single vat.
2. Problem - Currently, most 3D printed parts are made from a single material, leading to functional limitations.
3. Method - The study proposes a strategy for single-vat multimaterial VPP that selectively activates various chemical reactions using light.
4. Key Result - It demonstrates the potential to form complex structures through the expansion of resin chemistry, improved reaction selectivity, and grayscale and multiwavelength light control.
5. Takeaway - Multimaterial VPP technology could enable transformative applications in medicine, manufacturing, and aerospace.

title: Multimaterial additive manufacturing through grayscale digital light processing 3D printing
venue: Journal of Intelligent Material Systems and Structures
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the multimaterial additive manufacturing technology through grayscale digital light processing (g-DLP).
2. Problem - It aims to address the limitations of traditional digital light processing (DLP) and enable diverse property adjustments.
3. Method - The method involves modulating ultraviolet (UV) light intensity at the pixel level to tune properties within a single resin vat.
4. Key Result - g-DLP demonstrates the ability to adjust mechanical, optical, and electrical properties while maintaining high resolution and smooth surface quality.
5. Takeaway - The core message of this paper is that g-DLP enables the creation of advanced materials and devices for next-generation applications.

title: Multi-material integrated 3D-printed electrochemical detection platform for rapid on-site screening of nimesulide in industrial sewage
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses a multi-material integrated 3D-printed electrochemical platform for rapid on-site detection of nimesulide in industrial sewage.
2. Problem - It aims to resolve the limitations of existing detection methods regarding reproducibility and applicability in complex environments.
3. Method - The study involved the fabrication of a 3D-printed electrochemical platform using carbon black-filled polylactic acid electrodes and evaluating its electrochemical characteristics.
4. Key Result - The platform demonstrated a detection limit of 0.19 μM and a recovery rate of 90 ± 5%, showcasing high reproducibility and selectivity.
5. Takeaway - This research highlights the practical potential of a customizable multi-material integrated 3D-printed electrochemical detection platform for sustainable wastewater monitoring.

title: Investigating the Reliability and Dynamic Response of Fully 3D-Printed Thermistors
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper explores the reliability and dynamic response of fully 3D-printed multi-material thermistors.
2. Problem - There is a lack of foundational data to enhance the measurement capability and dynamic performance of thermistors.
3. Method - Thermistors were fabricated using FDM and micro-dispensing techniques, comparing different designs.
4. Key Result - The thermal indexes for D1 and D2 thermistors were recorded at 905.64 K and 813.03 K, respectively, with comparable dynamic performance.
5. Takeaway - Improving the surface properties of the substrate is essential for enhancing the performance of 3D-printed thermistors.

title: InFuse: In-Situ Material Injection for 3D Printing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses InFuse, a hybrid manufacturing technique that combines in-situ material injection with 3D printing.
2. Problem - It aims to overcome the limitations of the traditional 'printing-then-injection' approach.
3. Method - A novel volume decomposition algorithm based on a directed acyclic graph (DAG) and an interactive design tool for custom model control were utilized.
4. Key Result - InFuse demonstrated effective and reliable results across geometries with varying levels of complexity.
5. Takeaway - The core message of this paper is that InFuse enables rapid fabrication of complex geometries and multi-material composites.

title: Hybrid epoxy–acrylate resins for wavelength-selective multimaterial 3D printing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses hybrid epoxy-acrylate resins for wavelength-selective multimaterial 3D printing.
2. Problem - Existing 3D printing materials lack the capability for wavelength selectivity.
3. Method - The study employs the development of hybrid epoxy-acrylate resins that exhibit properties responsive to various wavelengths.
4. Key Result - The developed resins demonstrate excellent selectivity across different wavelengths, expanding the possibilities for multimaterial printing.
5. Takeaway - This research suggests that the development of 3D printing materials with wavelength-selective functions can drive innovation in multimaterial printing.

5. Takeaway - The research enables simultaneous printing of multi-gradient materials while avoiding structural defects that traditional methods cannot prevent.

ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - It aims to solve the challenges of producing low-cost and high-performance electromagnetic reciprocating micropumps.
3. Method - The study employs a new 3D model design and a tailored fabrication workflow for efficient micropump production.

5. Takeaway - The key message is that multi-material jetting 3D printing offers significant potential for low-cost, high-performance miniature micropumps.

title: Grayscale 4D Printing of Ferromagnetic Soft Materials
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the grayscale 4D printing technology of ferromagnetic soft materials.
2. Problem - Existing multi-material systems struggle to balance mechanical properties, leading to complexity and slower manufacturing speeds.
3. Method - The approach combines digital light processing (DLP) grayscale 3D printing with ferromagnetic particles in a single-material system for localized mechanical property programming.
4. Key Result - The technique achieves a load-bearing capacity of up to 42.6 times its weight and an improvement of 98.6% in bending angles, demonstrating rapid responsiveness.
5. Takeaway - This study offers a streamlined approach to ferromagnetic 4D printing, expanding the potential for advanced material applications without complex multi-material processes.

ai_summary_en:

3. Method - A comparative analysis was conducted focusing on smart adaptable materials and sustainable additive manufacturing techniques between traditional devices and innovative prototypes.
4. Key Result - The results indicate that artificial intelligence plays a crucial role in advancing smart assistive devices through decentralized additive manufacturing in hospitals.
5. Takeaway - The paper emphasizes that smart and sustainable assistive devices can outperform conventional solutions and promote equitable access for all users.

title: Exploring the mechanical, biological and degradation properties of PVA and PETG for engineering multi-material 4D printed actuators triggered by degradation
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper explores the mechanical, biological, and degradation properties of multi-material 4D printed actuators.
2. Problem - It aims to overcome the limitations of existing research in developing actuators triggered by degradation.
3. Method - The study systematically investigates the combination of structural polyethylene terephthalate glycol-modified (PETG) and degradable polyvinyl alcohol (PVA).
4. Key Result - It was found that underwater erosion of PVA induces time-dependent triggering through loss of mechanical integrity, while PETG enables controlled actuation in aqueous environments.
5. Takeaway - This research presents new possibilities for the development of sustainable and adaptive 4D printed materials.

title: Evaporation-driven generic, high-throughput and roll-to-roll printing of nanomaterials
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the evaporation-driven printing (EDP) method for high-throughput manufacturing of nanomaterials.
2. Problem - Conventional printing methods for nanomaterials have limitations in achieving large-scale uniform films due to specific physicochemical property requirements.
3. Method - The EDP approach utilizes the phenomenon of water evaporation to drive the rapid mobility and assembly of nanomaterials into multifunctional composite films.
4. Key Result - EDP-manufactured graphene oxide films demonstrate over 95.0% rejection for sodium sulfate, outperforming most graphene oxide-based counterparts.
5. Takeaway - The paper conveys that the EDP method opens new possibilities for the mass production of various nanomaterials, enabling the creation of functional films.

title: Evaluation of Bond Strength in Multi-Material Specimens Using a Consumer-Grade LCD 3D Printer
venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the evaluation of bond strength in multi-material specimens using a consumer-grade LCD 3D printer.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the issue of the lack of low-cost personal stereolithography printers with multi-material printing capabilities in the market.
3. Method - The study verified the suitability of currently available resins through printing, secondary curing, and tensile tests.
4. Key Result - The specimens produced by multi-material printing exhibited tensile strengths comparable to those of single-material specimens.
5. Takeaway - Multi-material printing using existing commercial resins is sufficiently practical in terms of strength, contributing to the realization of low-cost yet high-precision additive manufacturing technology.

ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the energy-efficient optimization of digital twin air handling unit systems based on indoor people counting.
2. Problem - It aims to resolve the issue of energy waste caused by traditional air handling units that do not adapt to varying demand.
3. Method - The study employs IoT technology alongside MobileNetSSD and NMS algorithms to gather people flow data, and develops a dynamic load prediction model using ANN.

5. Takeaway - The core message is that dynamically adjusting air supply rates in response to changing cooling loads can significantly enhance energy efficiency.

title: Acoustic Analysis of 3D Printing Motion Patterns for Machine Condition Monitoring
venue: SINTEK JURNAL Jurnal Ilmiah Teknik Mesin
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the analysis of mechanical vibrations and their acoustic emissions during the 3D printing process to establish a foundation for machine condition monitoring.
2. Problem - The vibrations during printing adversely affect dimensional accuracy and interlayer adhesion, highlighting the need for effective process monitoring.
3. Method - The study utilized five fundamental motion patterns fabricated on an FDM 3D printer, capturing acoustic emissions with two microphones and analyzing them in the time domain.
4. Key Result - The vertical toolpath exhibited the lowest RMS and Crest Factor values, indicating the most stable acoustic emission, confirming the influence of motion geometry on the printer's acoustic signature.
5. Takeaway - Time-domain acoustic analysis is a viable technique for characterizing machine performance, laying the groundwork for future real-time sound-based monitoring systems.

5. Takeaway - The findings demonstrate the potential of combining thermodynamic modeling with AI-driven methodologies to enhance plate heat exchanger performance in tropical environments like Uganda.

title: Volumetric Additive Manufacturing of Dormant Catalytic Chemistries to Generate Silicone Micro‐ and Millifluidic Devices and Instant Molds
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the use of tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing (T-VAM) for creating silicone micro- and millifluidic devices and instant molds.
2. Problem - It aims to overcome the limitations of photoactivated dormant catalytic chemistries that are incompatible with traditional layer-based additive manufacturing.
3. Method - A zero-dose optimization strategy is employed to preserve dormant catalysts in specific regions by avoiding light exposure.
4. Key Result - Micro- and millifluidic devices and instant molds were successfully produced using photoactivated dormant platinum photohydrosilylation catalysts.
5. Takeaway - Zero-dose optimization expands the range of accessible chemistries for VAM, enabling rapid fabrication of complex devices.

5. Takeaway - Thus, the paper presents a novel strategy to enhance design freedom in tomographic volumetric 3D printing.

title: Time-dependent volumetric printing of precision lenses through dynamic laser writing
ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - It addresses challenges in controlling dimensional accuracy in current vat photopolymerization-based additive manufacturing.

5. Takeaway - The findings suggest significant potential for achieving much smaller form errors in 3D printing of precision lenses compared to existing methods.

title: Thermal and Chemical Characterization of Digital Light Processing (DLP)-Manufactured Polymer Composites Reinforced with Jute Fibers
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper explores the thermal and chemical characteristics of jute fiber-reinforced polymer composites manufactured using Digital Light Processing (DLP).
2. Problem - It aims to address the challenge of developing sustainable materials with adjustable thermal and structural properties.
3. Method - Samples were created using UV-curable acrylate resin with varying jute fiber content, analyzed through TGA, TMA, DMA, and FTIR techniques.
4. Key Result - The study found that increasing fiber content led to a decrease in initial degradation temperature, reduced thermal expansion coefficients, and confirmed fiber-matrix chemical interactions.
5. Takeaway - Jute fibers demonstrate potential as a sustainable reinforcement, opening avenues for ecological and functional applications in 3D-printed composites.

title: Tailoring the Functional Properties of NiTi Shape Memory Alloy by Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process Conditions for 4D Printing
venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the tailoring of functional properties of NiTi shape memory alloy using the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process.
2. Problem - It aims to resolve the limitations in understanding the effects of LPBF process conditions on the properties of NiTi alloys.
3. Method - Thin-walled samples were manufactured from pre-alloyed NiTi powder via LPBF, employing a single track scanning strategy to isolate the pure effects of the laser.
4. Key Result - The established relationships between NiTi properties and LPBF process conditions provide a basis for developing production protocols with controlled functional properties.
5. Takeaway - This study highlights the potential to adjust the properties of NiTi alloys through laser influence.

5. Takeaway - This work opens a new avenue for biomimetic helices with multifunctionality.

title: Stiff and self-healing hydrogels by polymer entanglements in co-planar nanoconfinement
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a stiff and self-healing hydrogel using polymer entanglements.
2. Problem - It aims to address the issue that current stiffening methods suppress the chain/bond dynamics necessary for self-healing.
3. Method - The approach involves polymerizing a highly concentrated monomer solution within a co-planar nanoconfinement scaffold.
4. Key Result - The developed hydrogel exhibits a modulus of 50 MPa, tensile strength of 4.2 MPa, and a self-healing efficiency of up to 100%.
5. Takeaway - This paper presents a novel method for creating stiff and self-healing hydrogels, opening up various potential applications.

title: Spatiotemporally programmed dielectric liquid crystal elastomer: Electro-reversible 3D morphing via inverse 4D printing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the spatiotemporal programming of dielectric liquid crystal elastomers for electro-reversible 3D morphing.
2. Problem - It aims to address the challenge of achieving precise and reversible control over complex 3D deformations.
3. Method - A shear-assisted digital light-processing 4D printing strategy is employed to program the mechanical anisotropy of dielectric liquid crystal elastomers.
4. Key Result - The printed DLCE actuators exhibit multidimensional shape morphing under electric fields, demonstrating submillimeter-scale fidelity in reconstructing complex geometries.
5. Takeaway - This research highlights the potential of innovative shape-morphing materials for applications in soft robotics and adaptive systems.

title: Spatially programmed alignment and actuation in printed liquid crystal elastomers
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses spatially programmed alignment and actuation in printed liquid crystal elastomers.
2. Problem - It aims to address the effective control of alignment in liquid crystal elastomers and the associated performance limitations.
3. Method - The study combines experiments and modeling to analyze the effects of ink composition, nozzle geometry, and printing parameters on alignment.
4. Key Result - It was found that the uniformity of alignment varies with nozzle shape, and under certain conditions, the stiffness and actuation strain of printed LCEs significantly increase.
5. Takeaway - The key message of this paper is that by adjusting the flow rate during printing, LCE architectures with uniform composition can be realized.

title: Sparse-view irradiation processing volumetric additive manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses a volumetric additive manufacturing technique using sparse-view irradiation processing.
2. Problem - Traditional methods face limitations due to low projection efficiency and lengthy computation times.
3. Method - An optimized odd-even irradiation strategy inspired by sparse-view computed tomography was developed.
4. Key Result - High-quality fabrication was achieved with only 15 projections, enhancing projection efficiency by over 60 times.
5. Takeaway - The study significantly broadens the application of additive manufacturing in fields requiring rapid production.

ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - The lack of suitable manufacturing technologies has hindered the experimental validation of metallic twist metamaterials.

4. Key Result - It provides the first empirical evidence of rotation induced by compression in steel twist metamaterials.
5. Takeaway - The research highlights the sensitivity to manufacturing defects and suggests potential applications for twisted metamaterials.

venue: Volume 4: Gas Turbines; Pressure Technologies; Robotics & Automation

2. Problem - It aims to address the bulkiness of existing pneumatic actuators that require multiple units for multidirectional movement.

5. Takeaway - The research highlights the potential of advanced manufacturing and design innovation to enhance soft robotics.

title: Shape programming of liquid crystal elastomers by two-stage wavelength-selective photopolymerization
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the shape programming of liquid crystal elastomers through two-stage wavelength-selective photopolymerization.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the limitation of processability associated with existing base-catalyzed crosslinking methods.
3. Method - The approach utilizes a two-stage crosslinking procedure based on orthogonal wavelength-selective photo-initiation of free-radical and cationic ring-opening polymerizations.
4. Key Result - The method demonstrates improved processability compared to base-catalyzed procedures, enabling the manufacturing of complex shape-programmed materials.
5. Takeaway - The core message of this paper is that the new manufacturing method can significantly contribute to the development of complex shape-programmed materials.

title: Self‐Healing and Reprocessable Soft Robots Using 3D Digital Light Printing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses self-healing and reprocessable soft robots created using 3D digital light printing.
2. Problem - It aims to address the vulnerability of soft robots to mechanical damage due to their high compliance.
3. Method - The approach involves layer-by-layer polymerization using photoinitiated free-radical polymerization to create soft robots with complex air chambers.
4. Key Result - The resulting soft robots demonstrate excellent self-healing capabilities with efficiencies of 94.5% and 87.5% after damage.
5. Takeaway - This work highlights the potential for developing sustainable and resilient soft robots with complex geometries through additive manufacturing.

title: Resolving hydrophilic–hydrophobic resin mismatch for single-step volumetric additive manufacturing of cell-adhesive polyesters
ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - It aims to tackle issues arising from the incompatibility between hydrophilic and hydrophobic resins during the manufacturing process.
3. Method - The approach involves combining two different types of resins using volumetric additive manufacturing techniques.
4. Key Result - The study successfully produced cell-adhesive polyesters by effectively integrating hydrophilic and hydrophobic resins.
5. Takeaway - Thus, the core message of this paper highlights the potential of resin property adjustment in enhancing cell adhesion in volumetric additive manufacturing.

title: Resin properties and part size interrelationships in computed tomography-based volumetric additive manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the relationship between resin properties and part size in volumetric additive manufacturing (VAM).
2. Problem - It aims to resolve the dimensional limitations of printed objects produced through the VAM process.
3. Method - An analytical model is introduced to predict product size based on resin penetration depth, container size, and part formation duration.
4. Key Result - Significant correlations among these parameters were found, and experimental results closely matched analytical predictions.
5. Takeaway - The core message is that the penetration depth of resin plays a critical role in the VAM process, differing from traditional additive manufacturing methods.

title: Research on Laser Cladding Single-Pass Continuous Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Aluminum Matrix Composite Process Based on Abaqus
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the manufacturing process of continuous carbon fiber-reinforced aluminum composites using laser cladding.
2. Problem - It aims to resolve critical issues such as interfacial stress mismatch, fiber degradation, and unstable clad geometry during manufacturing.
3. Method - A dual-ellipsoid heat source-based thermoelastic-plastic finite element model was developed in Abaqus to simulate multi-physics interactions.
4. Key Result - The study identified optimal laser parameters that reduced fiber degradation by 42% and improved interfacial load transfer efficiency by 34.7%.
5. Takeaway - This research establishes a process-structure linkage framework for defect-controlled composite fabrication and provides a digital twin methodology for aerospace-grade manufacturing.

ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - It aims to resolve the misconception that complex designs incur no additional costs in additive manufacturing.

5. Takeaway - The study assists manufacturers and designers in quantifying the difficulty of part development at early stages for informed decision-making.

ai_summary_en:

2. Problem - The critical role of thermal debinding processes has been largely overlooked.
3. Method - The study employs a multi-distribution activation energy model and pattern-search methods to analyze resin pyrolysis kinetics.
4. Key Result - Monofunctional monomers effectively lower activation energy, facilitating pyrolysis and enabling high-quality debinding.
5. Takeaway - The findings serve as a reference for optimizing resin formulations to enhance debinding performance in ceramic VPP.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Fast Thermal Simulation in Laser Wire Additive Manufacturing
venue: 2025 15th France-Japan &amp; 13th Europe-Asia Congress on Mechatronics (MECATRONICS) / 23rd International Conference on Research and Education in Mechatronics (REM)
categories: AI and Machine Learning for AM
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for fast thermal simulation in Laser Wire Additive Manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the issue of traditional numerical solvers being too slow for mechatronic applications like real-time monitoring and model predictive control.
3. Method - The approach involves using PINNs to approximate thermal fields by minimizing PDE and boundary residuals directly.
4. Key Result - The proposed method enables accurate thermal simulation without meshing or time stepping, achieving a MAE of $\lt0.001^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.
5. Takeaway - This paper demonstrates that PINNs are a promising tool for efficiently performing thermal simulations in Laser Wire Additive Manufacturing.

title: Pellet-based 3D printing of soft thermoplastic elastomeric membranes for soft robotic applications
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses pellet-based 3D printing of soft thermoplastic elastomer membranes.
2. Problem - The challenge lies in the limited material range for 3D printing hyperelastic materials for soft robotics.
3. Method - The study explored the use of very soft thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) with Shore Hardness 00-30 in a pellet-based 3D printing approach.
4. Key Result - The thin membranes made from TPE can stretch up to 1320% and facilitate the design of a bending actuator capable of 180-degree bending.
5. Takeaway - The findings suggest that additive manufacturing with soft TPEs and membranes holds promise for soft robot applications.

title: Parallel Fin Ray Soft Gripper with Embedded Mechano-Optical Force Sensor
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a parallel soft gripper based on the Fin Ray effect with an embedded mechano-optical force sensor.
2. Problem - Integrating force sensors without compromising the flexibility and compliance of soft robotic systems is a significant challenge.
3. Method - The study employs a 3D printed gripper made from thermoplastic elastomers and proposes a sensor architecture utilizing a gyroid lattice structure.
4. Key Result - The proposed sensor achieves linear force measurements up to 150 N with an R2 value of 0.96 across two force regions.
5. Takeaway - This research contributes to the development of sensorized soft grippers that enhance force-sensing capabilities while retaining the benefits of soft robotic manipulators.

title: Oxygen Saturation as a Strategy to Mitigate User-Induced Variation in Tomographic Volumetric Additive Manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a strategy to mitigate user-induced variation through oxygen saturation.
2. Problem - It aims to address the inconsistency caused by user-induced variation.
3. Method - The study employs two different methods for preparing print vials to investigate oxygen concentration, followed by consecutive prints and analysis.
4. Key Result - Results indicate that oxygen concentration varies significantly with preparation method, and promoting oxygen diffusion in the print vial enhances printing consistency.
5. Takeaway - Thus, the core message is that oxygen saturation can improve consistency in additive manufacturing.

title: Optimizing Robotic Disassembly-Assembly Line Balancing with Directional Switching Time via an Improved Q(λ) Algorithm in IoT-Enabled Smart Manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the optimization of robotic disassembly-assembly line balancing in IoT-enabled smart manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the challenge of minimizing operation time while considering directional switching time during disassembly and assembly phases.
3. Method - An improved reinforcement learning algorithm, IQ(λ), is employed to manage non-conflicting parallel tasks and penalize inefficient task transitions.
4. Key Result - IQ(λ) consistently outperforms traditional Q-learning and Sarsa in terms of solution quality, convergence speed, and robustness.
5. Takeaway - This work provides a scalable and modular framework for intelligent scheduling in cyber-physical manufacturing systems.

title: Optical Properties of Gelatin Methacrylate and Implications for In Situ Cross-Linking in Spinal Cord Lesions and Engineered Hydrogel Systems
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the optical properties of Gelatin Methacrylate (GelMA) and their implications for in situ cross-linking in spinal cord injuries and engineered hydrogel systems.
2. Problem - There is a lack of data on the optical properties of GelMA, which is necessary to assess its cross-linking feasibility.
3. Method - The study measured the optical properties of GelMA using a double integrating sphere setup and conducted Monte Carlo simulations to analyze cross-linking under various illumination conditions.
4. Key Result - The research experimentally validated the feasibility of cross-linking GelMA in a spinal cord injury context based on its optical properties.
5. Takeaway - The findings support the potential for in situ photopolymerization in SCI repair and provide critical optical parameters relevant to bioprinting systems.

title: Observer-Based Volumetric Flow Control in Nonlinear Electro-Pneumatic Extrusion Actuator with Rheological Dynamics
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses volumetric flow control in a nonlinear electro-pneumatic extrusion actuator.
2. Problem - There is a need for consistent volumetric flow control when printing viscoelastic materials with complex rheological properties.
3. Method - A control framework is proposed that integrates simplified rheological dynamics using a Kelvin–Voigt model, nonlinear dynamic modeling, an unknown input observer (UIO), and a closed-loop PID controller.
4. Key Result - Simulation results validate the observer's accuracy, and experimental trials demonstrate the system's ability to achieve steady extrusion and maintain stable linewidth.
5. Takeaway - The proposed system offers a compact, sensorless solution well-suited for high-precision applications.

title: Non‐Sticky Display Eliminates Surface Roughness and Interface Adhesion: Enabling Large‐Scale LCD‐Based 3D Printing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses the use of a non-sticky display for large-scale LCD-based 3D printing.
2. Problem - It aims to address the issues of surface roughness and interface adhesion that hinder the adoption of LCD-based photopolymerization.
3. Method - The study employs a non-sticky display approach using a sub-micron structured polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) film laminated onto the LCD panel.

5. Takeaway - This research demonstrates the potential for advancing LCD VPP technology to develop functional parts.

2. Problem - It aims to address issues such as slow response times, the need for bulk stimulus exposure, and limited spatial precision in early 4D printing developments.
3. Method - The approach involves integrating functional nanoparticles into printable matrices to enable remote, localized, and highly programmable actuation.

5. Takeaway - The core message of this paper is that nanotechnology is unlocking new levels of functionality and adaptability in 4D printing.

title: Mechanical Characterization and Computational Analysis of TPU 60A: Integrating Experimental Testing and Simulation for Performance Optimization
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper explores the mechanical properties of thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) 60A and integrates experimental testing with simulation for performance optimization.
2. Problem - It addresses the challenge of understanding how different printing orientations and speeds affect the material's performance to identify optimal printing parameters.
3. Method - The study employed tensile tests according to ISO standards and conducted computational simulations using the finite element method.
4. Key Result - It was found that while 0° and quasi-isotropic printing orientations performed similarly, the quasi-isotropic orientation exhibited the most balanced mechanical behavior, making it the optimal choice.
5. Takeaway - The research provides comprehensive guidelines for soft robotics design and manufacturing, emphasizing the importance of tailored printing parameters.

title: Magnetic modulation of keyhole instability during laser welding and additive manufacturing
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses keyhole instability during laser welding and additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to solve the issues of keyhole collapse and pore formation caused by keyhole instability.
3. Method - High-speed X-ray imaging is used to demonstrate the critical role of flow vortex-induced protrusions on the rear keyhole wall in initiating instability.
4. Key Result - Applying a transverse magnetic field suppresses keyhole instability by driving a secondary thermoelectric magnetohydrodynamics flow that alters the net flow vortex.
5. Takeaway - The study emphasizes the significant impact of the relationship between laser scanning direction and magnetic field orientation on suppressing keyhole instability.

title: Magnetic beneficiation – A novel approach to facilitate additive manufacturing of lunar regolith ceramics by vat photopolymerization
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper discusses a magnetic beneficiation approach for lunar regolith ceramics in additive manufacturing.
2. Problem - The heterogeneous mineral composition and granulometry of lunar regolith create challenges during 3D printing and sintering.
3. Method - The study employs magnetic beneficiation of LHS-1 lunar regolith simulant to enhance printability and sintering behavior.
4. Key Result - Magnetic beneficiation reduced exposure time per layer by sixfold and improved sintered ceramic density by 10% and flexural strength by 30%.
5. Takeaway - The findings indicate that magnetic beneficiation is a promising strategy to enhance the performance of lunar regolith in additive manufacturing.

title: Lithography-based additive manufacturing of steel metamaterials: effect of sintering temperature on shape distortion, microstructure and mechanical properties
ai_summary_en:
1. Topic - This paper addresses the impact of sintering temperature on the shape distortion and mechanical properties of 316L stainless steel metamaterials in lithography-based metal manufacturing.
2. Problem - It aims to tackle issues related to high porosity and deformation during the sintering stage.
3. Method - The study conducts experiments by controlling the sintering temperature in a furnace designed for precise temperature management while using LMM for 3D printed metamaterials.
4. Key Result - Results indicate that a fully dense microstructure with high plasticity can be achieved within the 1300-1325 °C range, while exceeding this leads to distortion and brittleness.
5. Takeaway - The recommended sintering temperature range for 316L steel needs to be revised from the previously suggested 1360-1380 °C.
